pr_title: internal/initwd: follow local module path symlink
pr_body:
Fixes #21060

While a previous commit fixed a problem when the local module directory
contained a symlink, it did not account for the possibility that the
entire directory was a symlink.

I fully admit that the error phrasing is awkward and I enthusiastically welcome suggestions for improvement.

comments:
Hi @dblooman !
Thank you for reporting this, and providing a reproduction case! This will help me nail down where exactly terraform is looking for the relative paths to the modules.

I'm going to add a few notes here from my triaging - these are mostly meant to remind me what to look at next, so please don't worry that these notes don't provide an answer yet!

Using the repository you provided, I made the following change to `modules/services/demo/main.tf` and `terraform init` worked:

```
[kristin@fairy /tmp/terraform-bug:master *]
$ git diff modules/services/demo/main.tf
diff --git a/modules/services/demo/main.tf b/modules/services/demo/main.tf
index c8419ad..0d003c4 100644
--- a/modules/services/demo/main.tf
+++ b/modules/services/demo/main.tf
@@ -4,5 +4,5 @@ resource "aws_s3_bucket" "b" {
 }

 module "ami" {
-  source = "../../aws_example"
+  source = "../../../../modules/aws_example/"
 }
```

The trace log show where terraform is looking - note that the actual path relative is  `../../../modules/aws_example`:
```
2019/04/19 13:03:28 [TRACE] ModuleInstaller: testing.ami has local path "../../../../modules/aws_example/"
2019/04/19 13:03:28 [TRACE] ModuleInstaller: testing.ami uses directory from parent: ../../../modules/aws_example
2019/04/19 13:03:28 [DEBUG] Module installer: testing.ami installed at ../../../modules/aws_example
```

(edit: yes, I confirmed that `terraform init` works in this example as expected under 0.11.13)

There is a workaround that may or may not work for your actual situation, but it does work in the example repository. I changed the symlink from `modules/services` to the top-level `modules` directory:

Before:
```
$ ls -la modules
lrwxr-xr-x  1 kristin  wheel  22 Apr 19 13:31 modules -> ../../modules/services
```

After:
```
$ ls -la modules
lrwxr-xr-x  1 kristin  wheel  14 Apr 19 13:29 modules -> ../../modules/
```

And updated `main.tf` to point to the module in `./modules/services/demo`:

```hcl
 provider "aws" {}

 module "testing" {
    source = "../modules/services/demo"
 }
```

`terraform init` ran successfully after that.

Yeah, I guess that solution would work, I'm not sure if we are the edge case and should change or if there is a solution that means we don't have to, I will do some more testing to see how our tooling and scripts react to this change
@dblooman no worries - this is a bug and I fully expect to have this fixed before 0.12 is released.

I'm going to lock this issue because it has been closed for _30 days_ ⏳. This helps our maintainers find and focus on the active issues.

If you have found a problem that seems similar to this, please open a new issue and complete the issue template so we can capture all the details necessary to investigate further.
